He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

In a recent development, moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby reveals, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Sources indicate that moreira is presently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

Sources indicate that with four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.

The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s latest boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.

Frank has taken over an Eagles outfit that is sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 games and conceding a division-high 24 goals.

The Dane was believed to be on Palace’s radar in the summer, but he made it clear that he wanted an extended break away from management before assessing his options.

Frank now feels that the time is right to return to the Premier League “circus” for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February after a underwhelming eight-month spell in charge, winning just 34.2% of his 38 games in North London.

Remembered fondly for his successful seven-year tenure as Brentford boss, Frank is excited to take the reins at an “iconic” club in the form of Crystal Palace and is confident that he can steer them away from trouble.

Speaking at his first press conference on Thursday afternoon ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash at Coventry City, Frank told reporters: "It's good to be back! It's a little bit of surprise, the feeling I have in the body; how good it feels.

"Of course I stated yes for a reason, to join Palace and go back into the circus and into the Premier League.

"It's just so good to be back and I'm in no doubt there won't be times where it won't feel like that, but I'm happy to be here.".

"For me Palace is an iconic club in England and it's also shown that, in many years in the Premier League, doing fantastic things,” Frank added.

"Selhurst Park is a fantastic place to go, to watch football, to feel the atmosphere, to feel a proper game.

In a recent development, "I think Palace, when I've faced them over the years have always been a tough team to play. It's always been difficult.".

Frank was enjoying a break away from football in Australia with his family, but he was persuaded by Crystal Palace to return to the Premier League in the middle of a season.

In a recent development, "It's been of course extremely busy. In every aspect, of course, to join a pre-season is a privilege and I've had the privilege to do that in the other clubs I've been in,” remarked the Dane.

"The good thing is that you want to implement all your ideas, and that will take some time to hit the ground running, but I know what I want and the direction we should go in.

Industry observers note that "Timing - in life and football - is everything. I was enjoying my life in Australia. It's pretty nice down there. Nice weather together with the family. And I'm a person that really enjoys football, it is my life. It's scary to feel how I feel, how it feels to be back.

"I'll speak to my good friend Roy [Hodgson] of course and speak to him - I don't want to go as long as he did - but it's good, that feeling. Good to be back.".

Commenting on improving results at Selhurst Park and moving away from the relegation zone, Frank added: "I'm looking forward to come in to do everything I can to help the team, the club.

"I think it's a very talented squad. I think it's got good potential in every aspect.

"Of course we are in a position where we don't want to be, and I'll do my very best together with the staff and players to make sure we're in a much better position when the season is done.".

Crystal Palace, who have spent the last 14 years in the top flight, could climb out of the relegation zone if they end their four-match losing streak with a victory at Coventry this weekend and other results go their way.

Meanwhile, Frank has also provided a fresh injury upgrade on attacker Ismaila Sarr and defender Takehiro Tomiyasu ahead of their trip to the CBS Arena.

Pochettino will hold his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday afternoon, where he will provide an update on the team's injury situation.

#26487. Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's latest-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1637 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's latest-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.
  • It has been revealed that on the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.

It has been revealed that on the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did. They sat back, they were too cautious, and they lost. And yet, ever since, Tuchel has turned England into a free-scoring winning machine, topped off by a famous victory in Madrid, ending Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak.

It has been revealed that in the six games since the summer, England have scored 19 goals and conceded six. Five of those have been against the world champions.

Industry observers note that yes, this was the Nations League and not a World Cup semi-final. No, it wasn’t at the end of a gruelling five weeks of heat, humidity and altitude. And, yes, it was only a terrific late double save from James Trafford that stopped this being yet another tale of self-sabotaging England, thanks to Elliot Anderson’s red card, blowing another lead when under pressure.

But, this time, England did see it out. They secured Tuchel’s biggest win as England boss and, in doing so, demonstrated us just how he’s been able to get his side playing his way.

Harry Kane leads the England celebrations after his side's victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

Recent findings suggest that remember when everyone used to lose their minds whenever Harry Kane dropped deep in substantial games under Southgate? He’s our bloody striker, for goodness sake. Get in the box!

After England’s defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final two years ago, Opta posted on X that Kane had touched the ball just once in the opposition box across both that game and their previous final heartbreak against Italy three years earlier.

In a recent development, ‘One fewer than Jack Grealish,’ the post continued. ‘Grealish played 21 minutes in the 2020 final and didn't make the Euro 2024 squad.’.

It has been revealed that ballon d’Or winner Kane has made it quite clear since that he doesn’t need to spend all his time in the box to influence games. When he drops deeper, Kane is able to show the full extent of his creativity and range of passing.

Industry observers note that the main problem with the ploy under Southgate, however, was that Kane rarely had the team-mates to make the right runs ahead of him. He was surrounded by players who wanted to take up similar positions. Just look at the average position maps (below) from England’s loss to Spain at Euro 2024 compared to last night.

The average position map of England’s players in the loss to Spain at Euro 2024 show how Kane dropped deep, without team-mates making runs for him to exploit.

...whereas on Sunday night he had runners - Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers - around and beyond him.

Sources indicate that two years ago, the only player who averaged their touches ahead of Kane was Bukayo Saka. Jude Bellingham was out wide. Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden were basically in Kane’s shadow.

On Sunday night, he had Anthony Gordon, the brilliant, belligerent Bellingham and Morgan Rogers all ahead of him – and nearly even Ben White.

That desire, and instruction, to flock forward under Tuchel has made such a difference.

Recent findings suggest that take England’s third goal (below). Kane has the ball outside the area. Rogers is bombing on to his left. Gordon, who started as a winger but finds himself occupying the central spaces Kane leaves behind, darts into the box and points to where he wants it.

Sources indicate that bellingham is demanding the ball, too, showing Kane he wants it to feet. Even Anderson is charging into the box. Kane finds Bellingham, who feeds the unseen White, sprinting forward on the overlap to finish.

Kane picks up the ball and is met with an array of options in front of him, ahead of England's third goal.

He did similar in the win against Croatia a few days earlier, too.

Kane collects the ball deep with four bodies ahead of him, including full backs Lewis Hall and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It his raking pass to the back post which allows Bellingham to set up Rogers to finish.

Kane's lofted pass to Rogers (top right) leads to a goal against Croatia for Bellingham (edge of box).

Sources indicate that england’s fluidity in the final third is bamboozling defences. That is how you get the best of Kane’s creativity.

PLAYING LIKE A PREMIER LEAGUE SIDE.

Football is changing, so Pep Guardiola told us all in January last year. The modern game is now how teams like Bournemouth and Brighton play. The current Premier League table would suggest he had a point.

Over the past few years in the English top flight, we have seen teams move away from an obsession with keeping the ball for the sake of it and turn towards a far faster, more aggressive and more physical style of play.

It has been revealed that tuchel wants to take from that playbook. ‘We're at our best when we're free, physically overpowering and making it Premier League-level,’ stated Kane after last month's 7-0 rout of Croatia.

In the six matches since the World Cup, Tuchel’s England are having much less of the ball than they did at the start of his reign – and now less even than under Southgate.

It has been revealed that the key is they are becoming ever more direct with it. Tuchel wants his England to play out of the back with short passes, entice opponents on to them, but then move it through the lines at speed.

Recent findings suggest that since the World Cup, England are playing far fewer passes, but more of them into the box – to find those runners. A higher percentage of them forward. More direct attacks, moving the ball up the field at a quicker speed.

According to recent reports, on Sunday night, they showed how Tuchel wants his side to press. ‘We were hungry in the opposition half,’ said the England boss at full time.

A fine example of that (below) came just after just six minutes. Declan Rice gives his Arsenal team-mate Martín Zubimendi no time at all on the ball inside his own area, charging him down, and forcing him to play out to another Gunner in Mikel Merino. But he, too, is being harassed by Anderson and eventually England win it back and set up Kane for a chance that he fizzes wide.

A half-fit Rice was unable to apply that pressure in the summer.

Declan Rice charges forward to close down Martin Zubimendi who has possession just inside the Spanish box with Kane and Bellingham already engaged in a high press...

...Zubimendi passes to Mikel Merino but Elliot Anderson is all over him and it leads to Kane shot that just fizzes wide.

So much of this improvement under Tuchel into a side capable of blowing teams away can be put down to another abstract word he used post-match in Madrid: ‘brave’.

Tuchel talked in the last international break of ‘unlocking the next level’, and taking ‘calculated risks’ with a ‘man-to-man’ press in the opposition half.

Under Southgate, and certainly in the cowardly retreat against Argentina in the summer, England indicated little bravery either with the ball or without it and frequently showed too much respect to those massive nations.

Too safe with the ball, too afraid to give it away, and too fearful to try to win it back in case you leave yourself open.

It has been revealed that that appears to be changing, too. There was a moment at the start of the second half when Bellingham tried a risky through-ball to Rogers, which failed to find its man, instead of another simple ball out wide.

It handed Spain possession cheaply. But England didn’t care because they just pounced again. Spain couldn’t deal with it. In the first half, Spain completed just 84 per cent of their passes in their own half – a place where they are usually able to knock it about at will – their lowest completion rate according to Opta since the 2010 World Cup. They didn’t have a shot on target until the penalty.

England’s defence has long been seen as the weak spot and, under Southgate, it felt as though he always would rather his attacking talents not be too frivolous for fear of exposing it.

Thomas Tuchel and Kane direct England's players to keep on the front foot during the win over Spain.

Tuchel is doing the opposite. England’s expected goals soared from 1.7 per game under Southgate from the 2022 World Cup to the end of his reign, to 2.2 under Tuchel’s until this summer’s tournament. Since then, it’s jumped again to 2.8 but at the cost of what they are conceding. In his early days, England coughed up fewer good chances than under Southgate but since the World Cup has more than doubled.

He will want to get that down, of course, but when you are creating so much – and have an array of top finishers to see them off – how much will that matter to Tuchel?

According to recent reports, even he’s getting braver. His decision to take off Gordon for Konsa and chuck as many defenders on during England’s shrinking against Argentina looked a decision that would forever haunt Tuchel’s tenure.

Against Spain, Kane made way but Tuchel ended the game with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the pitch. Against Spain, he held his nerve.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.
  • Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.
  • By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.

Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.

By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.

The structure never worked. Amanda Staveley was bought out in July 2024. Dan Ashworth left for Manchester United.

Paul Mitchell lasted under a year, branded the transfer operation “not fit for purpose” and ended up in a turf war with Eddie Howe which was largely irrelevant as every financial decision was made by Saudi Arabia PIF. Mitchell might have identified the problem but he had no answers.

Darren Eales and Dan Ashworth struggled to get past PIF’s processes. Good football people kept failing inside this framework. At some point you have to blame the framework.

Recent findings suggest that I agree Eddie Howe came back much too early and fatigued mentally and physically. But he still delivered the Champions League football.

It has been revealed that last seasons 12th with 17 league defeats was a bitter pill swallow and faced with the new strategy and sale of his best players he walked away in July. He certainly was not at his best and was working with a divided squad where both Gordon and Tonali indicated to the club they were leaving before Christmas.

Sources indicate that the central glitch is our senior players simply had much higher earning potential at the six clubs who do not face the same SCR restrictions. Alexander Isak was reportedly assured of an improved deal by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi in March 2024. Paul Mitchell shelved it and Eddie Howe publicly cited PSR as the reason. Isak downed tools. Every dressing room and every agent drew the same conclusion: PSR then, SCR now, this club can’t pay you what you’re worth. So Gordon, Tonali and Bruno followed him out, with Trippier also gone.

Industry observers note that blaming Eddie Howe for transfers is a simplistic and nuanced view. None of the players signed in summer 2025 were his first choice, the embarrassing prolonged struggle to get transfers over the line are a clear manifestation of that. Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were signed two weeks after the season started in desperation. That after the board took direct control of the Alexander Isak situation and prevented Eddie Howe from communicating with the player.

Beware the convenient narrative. It was Amanda Staveley’s naivety, then Paul Mitchell’s manner, then Alexander Isak’s greed, then Eddie Howe’s stubbornness. Now it is Matthias Jaissle’s tactics or Ross Wilson’s signings. A new scapegoat every season is very useful to the people who never change. When the same problems outlast every individual blamed for them, the individuals were never the problem.

In a recent development, under Ross Wilson the upcoming model has seen eight of the summer’s signings being 24 or younger, including 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax for about £20m. Dortmund is the stated template. Roughly £249m of players went out. The CEO’s line is that anyone under contract leaves “on our terms.”.

According to recent reports, the problem is they still leave. Call it what it is: develop to sell. Under SCR, trading profit inflates the revenue side of the ratio, so I understand the logic.

Newcastle United are mid-table under Matthias Jaissle with the youngest squad in years. The question for Saudi Arabia PIF: is this a staging post at Newcastle United, or the destination?

  • A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:31.

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw across seven games in all competitions, Aston Villa have failed to come out on top in any of their last four matches (D2 L2), with their latest setback sparking a furious reaction from manager Unai Emery.

Villa allowed Man United to come from two goals behind twice and salvage a point in a chaotic 4-4 draw at Old Trafford prior to the international break, with the visitors conceding two goals in stoppage time to be denied what would have been just their third win at the Theatre of Dreams in 32 visits.

Three wins, four draws and three defeats have been posted by the Midlands club in 10 top-flight games this term, leaving them sitting 10th in the Premier League table and five points behind the top four where they finished last season.

Since the beginning of October, Villa have dropped a joint-division-high six points from winning positions, while their defensive concerns remain having conceded in 13 of their 16 matches across all competitions this season.

Heading into Emery’s 150th Premier League game in charge this weekend, Villa have found the net 14 times across a five-game unbeaten home run (W3 D2), while they have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight meetings with Sunderland (W5 D6) – a 3-1 away defeat in January 2016.

Sunderland ended a miserable seven-game winless run in the Premier League with a much-needed 1-0 triumph over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light before the international break, courtesy of a first-half penalty from Enzo Le Fee.

Head coach Regis Le Bris was delighted to see his Black Cats side ‘re-connect with our identity and our fans’ after delivering a gritty and disciplined display that helped them climb off the foot of the Premier League table for the first time in three weeks.

Now sitting 19th and only three points behind Hull in 13th spot, Sunderland will be looking to win consecutive top-flight games for the first time this season when they make the trip to Villa Park this weekend, as well as end their five-game winless streak on the road.

The Black Cats sit rock bottom of the away form table having accumulated only one point (D1 L4) and conceded a joint-division-high 13 goals, including three in a 3-1 defeat at Coventry City at the end of last month.

Sunderland now head to the Midlands seeking to end a seven-game winless run away against Aston Villa across all competitions (D3 L4), with their last victory at Villa Park coming in January 2011 when Phil Bardsley’s late strike secured a 1-0 Premier League triumph under Steve Bruce.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana – who signed a contract extension earlier this week – and Matteo Ruggeri both remain sidelined through injury, while Matty Cash is also out after picking up concussion on international duty with Poland.

Industry observers note that however, Johan Manzambi is available for selection after recovering from a calf problem, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka should also be ready to play after missing the last six games with a thigh injury. He could therefore compete with Taylor Harwood-Bellis for the right-back berth.

Recent findings suggest that nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and Alysson were all on the scoresheet at Old Trafford and will hope to retain their starting spots in the final third. Leon Goretzka also scored against Man United but he faces competition from Joao Gomes to start in centre-midfield alongside Boubacar Kamara.

As for Sunderland, Le Bris has confirmed that captain Granit Xhaka (calf) and striker Brian Brobbey (thigh) are ruled out due to injury, joining Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard and Habib Diarra (both thigh) in the treatment room.

However, Omar Alderete is back from a one-match suspension and could replace Luke O'Nein at centre-back, joining Trai Hume, Nordi Mukiele and Reinildo Mandava in defence.

Chemsdine Talbi was handed his first PL start of the season against Chelsea and will hope to continue on the left flank ahead of Nilson Angulo, while Wilson Isidor – who scored home and away against Villa last season – is set to lead the line in Brobbey's absence.

Sunderland possible starting lineup:.

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, Alderete, Reinildo; Ahoka, Sadiki; Meunier, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor.

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

While the Black Cats will be desperate to build on their victory over Chelsea as they bid to climb away from danger, the absence of both Xhaka and Brobbey is a real blow, and we expect Villa to ultimately navigate their way to a narrow triumph on home soil.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

In a recent development, rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

In a recent development, carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Industry observers note that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

In a recent development, equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

According to recent reports, carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

It has been revealed that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

It has been revealed that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager remarked. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Industry observers note that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Sources indicate that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and promptly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick mentioned: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13.
  • In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.
  • The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13.

In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.

The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.

Blackpool return to action on Saturday fresh off the dismissal of manager Evatt with the hopes of climbing away from the League One drop zone.

They endured a tough start to their first full campaign under Evatt, right now sitting 20th with just 12 points on the board from 13 games, winning three and losing seven of those.

The most recent of those victories came in October to end a six-game winless run in the third tier, but the Tangerines failed to build on it, going on to lose 4-1 to Mansfield and rescue a 1-1 draw against a Sheffield Wednesday side who played the second half with 10 men.

Then after scraping past non-league AFC Hornchurch in extra time in the FA Cup first round, they visited AFC Wimbledon last weekend and again came away empty-handed, having failed to find a leveller after Alistair Smith's 13th-minute.

That triggered the dismissal of Evatt by the club hierarchy on Thursday, and now under the temporary charge of Steve Thompson and only above the relegation zone on goal difference, they will be desperate to begin rebuilding confidence and a cushion over the bottom four with a much-needed home win.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to continue an upturn in form and their climb away from the relegation zone.

Wigan Athletic also endured a tough start to their League One campaign under Gary Caldwell, sitting bottom after 12 games with just seven points on the board having lost nine of those matches.

That was largely down to the Latics' struggles in attack, but they appear to have turned a corner since, winning two and drawing one of their last three league games while scoring five goals, firstly ending a three-game losing run by beating fellow strugglers Bromley 3-2.

Then following a stalemate with Mansfield Town and consecutive cup wins over Boreham Wood and Crewe Alexandra, Caldwell's men went into another notable contest at home to Barnsley on Saturday and won 2-1 as Fraser Murray put them ahead, Cameron McGeehan pegged them back and Jensen Weir scored the decisive goal 15 minutes from time.

Still with plenty of cause for concern in their away record, having drawn one and lost six of seven league games on the road, but finally with some momentum on their side, Wigan Athletic head to Bloomfield Road in search of a third win in four games to build on their two-point lead over the drop zone.

Blackpool form (all competitions):.

Wigan Athletic League One form:.

Wigan Athletic form (all competitions):.

Blackpool were hit by a sickness bug for last weekend's game, with Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe among those to miss out.

They may be back in contention for Saturday, while defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe remain sidelined alongside George Honeyman.

Karoy Anderson will head back from international duty with Jamaica but was in action in Mexico on Wednesday, while Dion Charles, Jerry Yates, CJ Hamilton and Niall Ennis will all compete for attacking places after Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham partnered up up top last time out.

Wigan Athletic will likely remain without forwards Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris due to ongoing injuries.

Scott Hogan is back in contention after a brief layoff and came off the bench last time out, but Caldwell may go unchanged from the Barnsley win, with Christian Saydee leading the line with support from Bradley Burrowes and Jon Mellish.

Murray will continue to offer attacking support in a wing-back role after his opener against Barnsley, while Weir and Max Power will continue in the middle of a 3-4-3 setup.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Southwood; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Niskanen, Morgan, Brown, Coulson; Bowler, Charles, Yates.

Wigan Athletic possible starting lineup:.

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, Murray; Burrowes, Mellish; Saydee.

Blackpool remain devoid of confidence and have been hit by injuries, illness and a managerial departure, but they still have more quality than their league standing suggests while the visitors have been poor away from home this season.

We see the Tangerines at least avoiding defeat against a resurgent Wigan team.

OLIVER HOLT: Why England CAN now end 62 years of hurt - Thomas Tuchel is intoxicating and I'd tip Jude Bellingham to beat Kylian Mbappe to the next Ballon d'Or... plus my top 10 Three Lions performances

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • The glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning.
  • For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.

The glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

For England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

According to recent reports, this was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

This felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain.

Once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

According to recent reports, for the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

This year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Industry observers note that yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain.

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it.

Industry observers note that and then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted organization of the other players on two fine teams.

Industry observers note that bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Sources indicate that bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

Recent findings suggest that he has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be said about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Recent findings suggest that harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or.

It has been revealed that with them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he demonstrated when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

According to recent reports, now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

Alan Shearer has been asked to name his all time Newcastle United starting eleven.

The United and England legend accepting the challenge.

Not a bad Newcastle United starting eleven….

The Premier League record goalscorer talking to All Out Football and starting at the back.

Alan Shearer: “Shay Given in goal, Trippier on the right, I’m going to say Dan Burn because he scored in the final and helped us lift the trophy. I’m going to say Lewis Hall as a left-back and as the other centre-half I’m going to say, value for money it has to be Fabian Schar.”.

The former NUFC number 9 then moving on to midfield: “Rob Lee, Bruno…”.

Industry observers note that then finally Alan Shearer getting to the top of the pitch: “Beardsley without a doubt, Newcastle’s best ever player. Ginola, me and Les Ferdinand.”.

So that makes it this all time Newcastle United starting eleven, according to Alan Shearer:.

Shay Given Kieran Trippier Fabian Schar Dan Burn Lewis Hall Rob Lee Bruno Guimaraes Peter Beardsley David Ginola Les Ferdinand Alan Shearer.

The AC Milan squad returned to training at Milanello on Monday, at least those who are not with their national team.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) has provided an revision on the various injuries that have massively depleted the depth available to head coach Ruben Amorim in the past few weeks.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical glitch that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

In a recent development, the Rossoneri captain took a knock to the hip area and felt some discomfort in his right adductor. No medical examinations were conducted while he was away, but they have been scheduled for early this afternoon.

Maignan has put the club at ease, stating that he is not in any pain. Yesterday evening, he posted a photo of himself preparing to make a save, perhaps a way of saying he is ready. However, Lorenzo Torriani is on stand-by if needed.

Meanwhile, yesterday afternoon, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek underwent examinations to assess their recovery from their respective muscle injuries. The tests took place in London, where both players spent the week off granted by the coaching staff.

The news is encouraging, and the recovery process is progressing well: the injury to the defender’s medial flexor in his right thigh is healing, and he will begin gradual work on the pitch over the coming days.

According to recent reports, whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

Telstar vs PEC Zwolle - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.
  • Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.
  • Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.

Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.

Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.

Industry observers note that A 10-match winless run between August 8 and October 23 dampened any optimism that may have been brewing after Telstar’s season-opening win over NEC. However, they have since responded with four points from a possible six, most recently earning a 2-2 draw against Fortuna Sittard.

Having been tipped by many as the next managerial casualty of 2026-27, Henk Brugge appears to have bought himself some breathing room, but he will know his position remains precarious, and any underwhelming result could still spell the end for him.

Averaging two goals per home league match this term, De Witte Leeuwen have found little difficulty scoring in front of their fans, although much of that good work is being undone by a porous defence that has conceded 17 times across six home games.

Industry observers note that january’s 4-1 defeat marked Telstar’s seventh straight loss against Zwolle and extended their winless run in this fixture to 16 matches across all competitions dating back to February 2007. This weekend’s hosts will need to buck an unpleasant trend to secure all three points.

A 4-2 triumph over FC Utrecht in their most recent home match ended a run of six games without a win for Telstar, who now seek back-to-back victories in Velsen for the first time since beating Sparta Rotterdam and Heracles by a combined score of 7-1 to close out 2025-26 on a high.

According to recent reports, after weeks of searching, PEC Zwolle will have a new face in the dugout for their upcoming clash against Telstar, with Alex Pastoor recently appointed as head coach until the end of the 2026-27 season. He replaces Henry van der Vegt, whose 15-month tenure ended in October.

Pastoor’s immediate task will be to build on his side’s four-game league unbeaten run, during which they have collected eight points from a possible 12, with only Heerenveen (12) and Ajax (10) boasting a better record in the division.

With three of their next four matches coming against teams at the moment in the top seven - AZ Alkmaar, Fortuna Sittard, and PSV Eindhoven - De Blauwvingers could use a win here as they look to put some distance between themselves and the drop zone before the end of 2026.

Both of Saturday’s opponents have managed just three clean sheets between them from 24 matches this season, so this weekend’s clash is likely to be decided at the attacking end. On that front, Zwolle have struggled compared to their hosts, scoring five fewer goals so far.

However, the visitors could tilt things in their favour with a quick start, and having scored the opener in four of the last five gameweeks, they may look to capitalise on a Telstar side that has conceded first four times during that span.

Telstar form (all competitions):.

PEC Zwolle form (all competitions):.

Gerald Alders, 21, has missed Telstar’s last four matches and will remain sidelined for Saturday’s clash as he continues his recovery to full fitness.

Rui Mendes is also unlikely to feature for the hosts, though his comeback is not far off after missing the last three matches.

Tyrone Owusu has four goals and one assist in his last six outings, already making this his most productive season in a Telstar shirt.

Deadline-day loan signing Filip Krastev has yet to feature this term due to an Achilles tendon injury sustained while playing for Goztepe.

Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus are also unavailable this weekend, but both are nearing their respective returns.

Telstar possible starting lineup:.

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Ahmed, Rossen; Martha, Owusu, Brouwer; Thorisson.

PEC Zwolle possible starting lineup:.

Schendelaar; Van der Haar, Viergever, Velthuis, Aertssen; Sommer, Thomas; Mbayo, Namli, Van der Wal; Van Hooijdonk.

Both teams have performed well of late, and neither enters Saturday’s game with their confidence depleted.

With little to separate the sides, a draw appears the most likely outcome, so we are backing a share of the spoils.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United host Arsenal on Saturday.

A 5.30pm kick-off against the Gunners.

All of the ‘experts’ taking for granted that Arsenal will win against Newcastle United.

The reigning champions having won nine of their ten Premier League matches and clear at the top, plus they haven’t conceded a single goal in their last seven hours of EPL football.

They say timing is the secret of great comedy.

Sources indicate that well, the timing of this football match is absolutely perfect for Newcastle United and it is no great secret. Not if you look hard enough.

There is something about this time of year at St James’ Park, darkness setting in, under the lights at SJP.

Something magical happens, time after time.

Here are the St James’ Park matches of recent seasons at this time of year….

2022-23 Newcastle 4 Aston Villa 0 (29 October 2022) Newcastle 0 Palace 0 and NUFC win 3-2 on penalties (9 November 2022) Newcastle 1 Chelsea 0 (12 November 2022).

2023-24 Newcastle 1 Arsenal 0 (4 November 2023) Newcastle 4 Chelsea 1 (25 November 2023_.

2024-25 Newcastle 2 Chelsea 0 (30 October 2024) Newcastle 1 Arsenal 0 (2 November 2024).

2025-26 Newcastle 2 Manchester City 1 (22 November 2025).

As you can see, a stunning set of results around this time of the year.

Especially our cockney friends, Arsenal and Chelsea, the cold dark nights on Tyneside and even better when it is a 5.30pm kick-off and a turbo alcohol charged crowd.

As fans, we just need to do our bit and let the dark and the cold do the rest!

Latest Update: Thomas Frank confirmed as Crystal Palace boss as he eyes raid on Chelsea set-piece guru marginalised under Xabi Alonso

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.
  • Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has taken a significant pay cut to take over at Palace, who languish at the bottom of the Premier League.

However, he will earn more than his predecessor, Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after winning just two of his ten league matches in charge.

It has been revealed that new Palace boss Frank noted: ‘It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

According to recent reports, ‘Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.’.

Across his spells at Brentford and Tottenham, Frank has managed 178 Premier League matches with a 34 per cent win rate.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager 🤝ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S pic.twitter.com/zv2vMPGPFz.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford.

Recent findings suggest that but Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is said Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

Sources indicate that cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their latest lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

According to recent reports, before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino sets out non-negotiables ahead of Man United bow at Anfield

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:39.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.
  • The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:39.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.

The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino officially started work as Red Devils head coach on Wednesday, having flown straight to England after managing his final USA game against Haiti.

The South American has taken charge of a team that presently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up just eight points from their first 10 games of the season.

Recent findings suggest that “It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free," Pochettino told Man United's official website.

According to recent reports, “The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most notable thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

"When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

According to recent reports, “That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero. I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.

Recent findings suggest that “To create the culture is the most notable [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create. We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.

“The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players.

According to recent reports, "We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”.

Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

According to recent reports, the Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.
